criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the implemented quorum logic against spec §1/§2 and found multiple send-back defects: same-provider seats are not collapsed at all (line 103), `seat_missing` / `evidence_mismatch` do not reliably force escalation or failsafe behavior because the resolution logic prioritizes agreement first (lines 117-123), `evidence_unverified` seats still participate in voting outcomes (line 78 plus later verdict aggregation), and shadow-seat concealment is not actually enforced despite being a design rule (line 150). These are core behavioral contradictions, not edge nits.

I checked for the required major pieces of the merge artifact: CLI parsing, seat-log loading, effective-status calculation, bundle-hash checks, flat/evidence-parity handling, divergence calculation, quorum record construction, legacy `claude`/`gemini` blocks, and log append flow. Those pieces are present and there are no TODO stubs or missing referenced files in this artifact. The main problems are incorrect implementations of some required rules rather than absent top-level sections.

I specifically checked the house/build conventions visible from the supplied spec: the file lives under `.claude/evals/`, quorum fields are additive, `agree` / `resolution` / `final_verdict` / `alex_ack` are preserved, and back-compat `claude{}` / `gemini{}` blocks are retained (lines 129-140). I did not find convention-level violations such as disallowed file placement, removed legacy fields, or obvious source-of-truth bypasses in this file.

I checked for the rubric's common build anti-patterns: over-engineered ceremony, duplicated state stores, tombstoned-tool resurrection, fabricated numbers, hardcoded secrets, and speculative platforming. The file stays lean and config-driven, reuses shared helpers (`calibration_stats`, `judge_lib`), and does not introduce those anti-patterns. The issues I found are logic/spec defects, not anti-pattern bloat.

I checked comments/help/error behavior for honesty and loud failures. The biggest issue is line 150: the CLI help says shadow verdicts are shown "only AFTER Alex has acked," but there is no enforcement, so the framing overclaims a protection the code lacks. Line 158 also returns success on an unknown-seat error, which weakens failure visibility for automation. Because the artifact's explanatory surface is materially more trustworthy than the code's behavior here, diagnostics falls below the pass line.

defects.quote: groups = {next(s.get("independence_group", s["id"]) for s in cfg if s["id"] == sid) for sid in voting}
defects.description: Spec §2 says, "Seats with the same provider or the same `independence_group` count as one vote." This code only collapses by `independence_group`; it ignores same-provider seats entirely. Two OpenAI seats with different or absent `independence_group` values could therefore count as independent votes and auto-pass when the spec says they must collapse to one opinion.

defects.quote: if agreed == "flag" and "verdict_mismatch" not in reasons:
defects.description: This branch auto-resolves any unanimous voting FLAG unless there is a verdict mismatch, even if `seat_missing` or `evidence_mismatch` is present. Spec §2 separately requires, "Advisory or voting seat missing, or bundle hashes differ ... -> escalated, or `failsafe_flag` ... | flag." Missing seats / evidence mismatch are supposed to force escalation or failsafe handling, not be bypassed by the all-flag shortcut.

This generic branch turns any agreed PASS with reasons into interactive `final = pass`. But spec §2 distinguishes reasons: for `seat_missing` and `evidence_mismatch`, the row says the final verdict is `flag`, not "pass pending ack." As written, a missing advisory/voting seat or differing bundle hashes can still yield an interactive PASS, which contradicts the table.

defects.quote: voting = {sid: r for sid, r in live.items() if effective[sid] == "voting"}
defects.spec_ref: §2 N-seat quorum rule; §6 Anti-rubber-stamp and anti-over-flag mechanics
defects.description: Spec §2/§6 says an `evidence_unverified:<seat>` result is "recorded, and its own flag / divergence no longer counts as a reason for THIS run." Here unverified seats are removed only from `advisory_flag` and divergence checks later on; they still remain in `voting`, so a voting seat tagged `evidence_unverified` can still create `verdict_mismatch` or help determine the agreed verdict. That gives the unverified seat escalation power the spec explicitly strips.

defects.quote: ap.add_argument("--reveal-shadow", action="store_true", help="show shadow seats' verdicts (only AFTER Alex has acked)")
defects.spec_ref: Summary item 3; §1 Seat role and trust ladder
defects.description: The spec says a shadow seat is "hidden from you until after you ack, so your label stays uncontaminated." This flag is documented as post-ack only, but the code does not check `alex_ack` or any other ack state before honoring it. A caller can reveal shadow verdicts early, defeating the contamination guard.

defects.quote: ap.add_argument("--reveal-shadow", action="store_true", help="show shadow seats' verdicts (only AFTER Alex has acked)")
defects.description: The help text promises an enforcement boundary ("only AFTER Alex has acked") that the program does not actually enforce. Under the rubric, a docstring/help string promising a property the code does not have is dishonest framing and harms maintainability/reviewer trust.

defects.quote: print(f"unknown seat '{sid}' (not in seats.json)", file=sys.stderr); return 0
defects.description: An unknown-seat/configuration error exits 0 and emits no quorum record or machine-readable resolution. That makes a real setup failure easy for automation to miss; the failure is visible only in stderr, so this path is not as loud/specific as the rest of the tool's contract.
